period: New Kingdom, 18th Dynasty, probably Amarna period, c. 1335-1323 BC
summary: The child king rising from a blue lotus like the newborn sun: the only known image of Tutankhamun as a child, with a whiff of scandal attached.
look: A head of painted wood and stucco, 30 centimetres tall, rising from a blue lotus flower on a blue base that stands for the primeval waters. The head is shaved, with painted black stubble, dark blue eyebrows and eyeliner, pierced ears and the long skull and neck creases of Amarna art. The red paint of the skin is damaged in large patches.
story:
Egyptian myth told that at the beginning of time a lotus rose from the dark waters, and from it came the young sun, as the child-god Nefertem. The lotus closes at night and opens again at dawn, so it became the flower of the sun's daily rebirth. Showing the king as Nefertem was a magical guarantee that he, too, would be reborn.

It is the only known image of Tutankhamun as a child. The elongated head and wrinkled neck are typical of Amarna art, which suggests it was made in the Amarna period, when he was still called Tutankhaten.

Then the scandal. Carter did not record it in his first-season notes, and there is no photograph of it in the tomb, unlike almost everything else. In 1924, while Carter was locked in a dispute with the authorities and away from Egypt, Pierre Lacau and Rex Engelbach of the Antiquities Service found it in KV4, the tomb of Ramesses XI, which Carter used as a storeroom. It was packed among bottles in a box of red wine. Carter later said it came from the rubble of the entrance corridor and simply had not been registered yet. Some still suspect he meant to keep it. Carter blamed the damage to its paint on the seizure.
details: Look at the ears: pierced, just like those of the gold mask.
Look closely at the scalp: black painted dots for stubble on a shaved head.
Find the blue base under the lotus: the primeval waters from which the world began.
Notice the long skull and creased neck, hallmarks of the Amarna style of Akhenaten's reign.
fun_fact: In 1924 inspectors found this head in a tomb Carter used as a storeroom, packed in a box of red wine bottles. Carter's explanation: he simply hadn't registered it yet.
narration: This is the boy king as the newborn sun. A child's head rises from an opening blue lotus, in painted wood and stucco, about 30 centimetres tall. Egyptian myth said that at the start of time a lotus rose out of the dark waters, and from it came the young sun god, Nefertem. Because the lotus closes at night and opens at dawn, it promised rebirth every morning. Showing Tutankhamun as Nefertem guaranteed that he too would be reborn. It is the only known image of him as a child, and the long head and creased neck are Amarna style, so it was probably made when he was still called Tutankhaten. Now the scandal. Carter never recorded it in his notes. In 1924, during a quarrel between Carter and the authorities, inspectors found it in a side tomb Carter used as a storeroom, packed in a box of red wine bottles. Carter said it came from the rubble in the entrance corridor and simply had not been registered yet. Some still suspect he meant to keep it. Look at the ears: they are pierced, just like those on the gold mask.

summary: More than 200 jewels, 143 objects on the body alone, and a pectoral whose green scarab is glass made by a cosmic impact in the Sahara.
look: The cases hold pectorals, collars, bracelets, rings and earrings in gold, inlaid with carnelian, lapis lazuli, turquoise and coloured glass. Find the chest ornament with a winged scarab at its centre: the scarab is pale yellow-green Libyan desert glass. Above it, a little boat carries the eye of Horus beneath the moon.
story:
The tomb held more than 200 pieces of jewellery. The mummy alone carried 143 objects in its wrappings: amulets, collars, bracelets, rings, two daggers, sandals and gold caps for fingers and toes. Many more lay in boxes in the Treasury and elsewhere, though ancient robbers had rifled them. Carter found a bundle of gold rings knotted into a cloth, apparently loot abandoned by a thief in a hurry.

The star is the pectoral with the winged scarab. Its body is carved from Libyan desert glass, a natural glass found in the eastern Sahara, in the deserts of western Egypt and eastern Libya. It formed about 29 million years ago. Its origin was long argued over, but recent research ties it to a meteorite impact: grains inside the glass show a mineral transformation that has only been found at impact sites. The Italian mineralogist Vincenzo de Michele published the identification of the scarab in 1998. Prehistoric people knapped the same glass into tools.

The scarab beetle rolls its ball of dung the way the sun god rolls the sun into the sky each morning, so a winged scarab is sunrise itself. Above it, a boat carries the eye of Horus under the moon. Sun below, moon above: day and night guarding the king.

The jewellery also tells you about the person. His ears were pierced, as you can see on the gold mask, and earrings were among the finds.
details: Find the winged scarab pectoral: the yellow-green scarab is Libyan desert glass, about 29 million years old.
Above the scarab, look for the boat carrying the eye of Horus under a moon disc and crescent.
Look for the broad gold collars in the shape of a vulture and a falcon, laid on the mummy for protection.
Spot the earrings: Tutankhamun's ears were pierced, as the gold mask shows.
Look for the gold finger and toe caps that were fitted to each finger and toe of the mummy.
fun_fact: The scarab on the king's chest is glass born about 29 million years ago when something from space struck the Sahara: Tutankhamun wore a piece of a cosmic accident.
narration: These cases hold Tutankhamun's jewellery, and there is a lot of it: more than 200 pieces in the tomb, and 143 objects on the mummy alone, tucked into the layers of linen. Collars, amulets, bracelets, rings, even gold caps for each finger and toe. Robbers got into the jewellery boxes in antiquity, and some loot never left the tomb: Carter found gold rings knotted into a cloth, apparently dropped in a hurry. Now look for the chest ornament with a winged scarab in the middle. The scarab beetle rolls its ball of dung the way the sun god rolls the sun into the sky each morning, so a scarab with wings is sunrise itself. But this scarab is special. Its pale yellow-green body is not a gemstone. It is Libyan desert glass, a natural glass from the Sahara between Egypt and Libya. It formed about 29 million years ago, and recent research ties it to the impact of a meteorite. So the king wore a piece of a cosmic accident on his chest. You will be in the Western Desert yourselves, at Siwa, in a couple of days. Above the scarab, a little boat carries the eye of Horus under the moon: sun below, moon above, day and night protecting him. One last detail: Tutankhamun's ears were pierced, and earrings were found in the tomb. Look at the scarab again and notice its soft green colour, the colour of glass born in fire.
